## Natural history notes

An aquatic to semi-aquatic fern with highly variable fronds that may float on the water surface or emerge above it. Water Fern often has broad, lobed sterile fronds and more finely divided, feathery fertile fronds that bear sporangia and produce spores. It grows in shallow, slow-moving or still freshwater habitats such as ponds, canals, ditches, marshes, and wetlands. In Florida, it occurs mainly in the peninsula and is considered a naturalized non-native species, likely introduced through the aquarium and ornamental pond trade.
